issue: Under U.S.S.G. § 2B1.1(b)(16)(A), must the government prove that the defendant subjectively knew of and consciously disregarded the risk of death or serious bodily injury, or is an objective risk sufficient?

sides.position: The defendant must have subjective awareness of the risk of death or serious bodily injury (the defendant-friendly test).
cases: United States v. Wala, 166 F.4th (6th Cir.) (pin 604) (declining to choose sides; assuming this test applies)
United States v. Reina Chirinos de Urena, No. 25-5976 (6th Cir. 2026) (assuming this test applies without deciding)

sides.position: The enhancement does not require proof that the defendant subjectively knew of the risk; an objective risk of death or serious bodily injury suffices.

quote: There, we declined to take sides in a “circuit split regarding whether the defendant must have a subjective awareness of the risk.”
cite: United States v. Reina Chirinos de Urena, No. 25-5976 (6th Cir. 2026)
